description.narrative: Folkräkning planeras till 1 april 2014. Gemensam fond med flertal givare via UNFPA.
Population census planned for 1 April 2014. Pool fund with several donors channeled through UNFPA.

The Population Census 2014 has produced accurate, reliable data on the demographic and socio-economic characteristics and have produced all thematic reports etc that it set out to do. This, the last year of the Census process has been used to mainly further disseminate data and to make data widely available for both the public as well as professionals.

Myanmar conducted a Population and Housing Census in March/April 2014, a first one in 30 years. The Department of Population (DOP) in the Ministry of Labour, Immigration and Population (MOLIP) was the lead government agency for the census, while UNFPA provided technical support. The Census was conducted with financial support from Australia, Finland, Germany, Italy, Norway, Sweden, Switzerland and the United Kingdom. The Census was conducted at an opportune time when Myanmar was embarking on socio-economic and political reforms and accurate, up-to-date disaggregated (geographic and social characteristics) data would be an important building block for these reforms. The census data was widely disseminated through printed reports: Union, State/Region, Township level (Total of 409 reports for townships and sub-townships) and a total of 14 thematic reports. Data were also disseminated through electronic platforms such as websites (DOP website, UNFPA website, MIMU and other websites), where all the printed materials as well as Microsoft Excel files of all data tables were posted. It is a unique feature of the 2014 Myanmar Census that the data has been disseminated on township level to a variety of stakeholders. To further build the capacity of data users at the township level, UNFPA and DOP also undertook Township dissemination workshops where township stakeholders discussed the census findings for their respective townships. This was done in collaboration with local NGOs with expertise in participatory approaches to capacity building. In 2017, up to 294 (out of total 330) townships were covered, reaching a total of about 18,000 township stakeholders. The remaining 36 townships could not be covered due to challenges of access (conflict and weather). At the end of the mulit-donor supported project in 2017, some dissemination and capacity building activities still remained to be done. These included dissemination workshops in the remaining townships and the production of additional electronic products that were depending on clean data sets which would only be available at the completion of the thematic analysis. In light of the pending activities, Sweden (as only donor) supported UNFPA with a cost extension for the full year 2018 to enable the completion of the activities.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
